overview.headline: Opposition to Constitution led to demand and ratification of rights amendments

keyPoints.point: 12 amendments were proposed and 10 ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791
keyPoints.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyPoints.point: The amendments defined citizens rights in relation to newly established government
keyPoints.quote: They defined citizens' rights in relation to the newly established government under the Constitution.

keyPoints.point: Memory of British violation of civil rights shaped opposition before and during Revolution
keyPoints.quote: Fresh in their minds was the memory of the British violation of civil rights before and during the Revolution.

keyPoints.point: Opponents demanded a bill of rights to spell out immunities of individual citizens
keyPoints.quote: They demanded a "bill of rights" that would spell out the immunities of individual citizens.

keyPoints.point: The first amendment concerned number of constituents for each Representative and was never ratified
keyPoints.quote: The first amendment, which concerned the number of constituents for each Representative, was never ratified.

keyTerms.gloss: The first 10 ratified amendments protecting citizens rights
keyTerms.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyTerms.gloss: Newly established government framework defining citizens relation to rights
keyTerms.quote: They defined citizens' rights in relation to the newly established government under the Constitution.

keyTerms.gloss: Fear that central government would open way to unchecked power
keyTerms.quote: would open the way to tyranny by the central government

keyTerms.gloss: Elected member representing a number of constituents in Congress
keyTerms.quote: The first amendment, which concerned the number of constituents for each Representative, was never ratified.
